strings.name: Martina Navratilova
strings.role: Tennis player · Singles and doubles champion
strings.summary: Raised in Czechoslovakia, Navratilova sought asylum in the United States in 1975. Her serve-and-volley tennis, fitness preparation and competitive longevity reshaped the women's game. She won 18 major singles and 31 women's doubles titles. Her rivalry with Chris Evert defined an era; after retirement she remained a broadcaster and participant in public debate.

strings.highlights.h1.title: Nine Wimbledon singles titles
strings.highlights.h1.text: Won nine times between 1978 and 1990, establishing the Wimbledon singles record.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Achievement across disciplines
strings.highlights.h2.text: Won 59 majors across singles, women's doubles and mixed doubles.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Celebrated her seventieth birthday
strings.timeline.t1.text: Gathered with family and tennis peers including Evert and Shriver, remaining active in tennis life.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Final major title
strings.timeline.t2.text: Won US Open mixed doubles with Bob Bryan and then ended her professional playing career.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Entered the Hall of Fame
strings.timeline.t3.text: The International Tennis Hall of Fame recognized her singles, doubles and lasting contribution.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Ninth Wimbledon victory
strings.timeline.t4.text: Won her final major singles title.
strings.timeline.t5.title: An 86–1 season
strings.timeline.t5.text: Completed an exceptional season and a career singles Grand Slam at the US Open.
strings.timeline.t6.title: First Wimbledon title
strings.timeline.t6.text: Defeated Evert in the final and reached world No. 1 for the first time.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Sought asylum in America
strings.timeline.t7.text: After the US Open, left Czechoslovakia's system and began a new professional and personal chapter.
strings.timeline.t8.title: National champion
strings.timeline.t8.text: Won Czechoslovakia's national championship at fifteen before moving onto the international professional stage.
